overview: Wind turbine service technicians, often called wind techs, keep wind farms running. They climb turbine towers to inspect, maintain and repair mechanical, hydraulic and electrical systems, and troubleshoot problems with generators and controls. O*NET rates mechanical knowledge at 4.54 out of 5 for this job and computers and electronics at 4.15. Most complete a technical school program, 34% report a certificate in O*NET data, plus on-the-job safety training. The BLS May 2025 median is $64,120, but it is a small field with 9,980 jobs. The job means heights, outdoor work in all weather and physical risk.
pay: Wind techs earn a median of $64,120, and the top 10% earn $92,460 or more. New York has the highest state median at $81,330, 27% above the national figure. Texas has by far the most jobs, 3,890, at a median of $61,950, followed by Iowa with 900 jobs at $74,880.

faq.q: How much do wind turbine technicians make?
faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $64,120 a year. The middle half earn between $58,840 and $78,010. New York, Kansas ($78,240) and California ($77,910) pay the most. Travel jobs often add per diem and overtime on top of base pay.

faq.q: How do you become a wind turbine technician?
faq.a: Most attend a wind energy program at a technical school or community college. In O*NET data, 34% have a post-secondary certificate, 22% some college and 29% a high school diploma. Employers train you in climbing, rescue and electrical safety, and there are 4 related programs.

faq.q: Is being a wind tech dangerous?
faq.a: It carries real risk. In O*NET data the job ranks at the top of all U.S. jobs for outdoor work and above 99% for physical risk. You work at great heights near high voltage, so strict safety procedures and cautiousness are essential.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to wind turbine technician?
faq.a: Hydroelectric Plant Technicians are a 92% match and earn a median of $102,040. Powerhouse and substation electrical repairers are an 89% match and earn $103,020, 61% more, according to BLS May 2025 data. Both use the same mechanical and electrical skills.
